claims.text: At stage-2 Order.CustomerId, PlacedAt, Status, Items and Version have private setters; Id has a public setter; Order has a private parameterless constructor and one public constructor (int customerId, List<OrderItem> items, DateTimeOffset placedAt).
A private setter ({ get; private set; }) lets any code read the property but only code inside the declaring class assign it.
claims.source_hint: C# docs: Properties; Restricting accessor accessibility

claims.text: EF Core cannot bind navigations (such as Items) to constructor parameters; it binds only mapped properties, a fixed rule of EF Core. So it cannot use Order's public constructor, whose items parameter matches the Items navigation.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Entity types with constructors; verified: stage-2 model without Order() throws 'No suitable constructor... Cannot bind items... Navigations cannot be bound'

claims.text: EF Core can use a private parameterless constructor and fill properties with private setters of mapped classes, which other classes cannot; at stage-2 the constructor binding for Order is the private Order() with 0 parameters.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Entity types with constructors; verified: DonHangDbContext model built from git archive stage-2, ConstructorBinding = private .ctor()

claims.text: EF Core maps a property whose setter is private and fills it with the column value when it loads a row (and writes it on save); Status is mapped with e.Property(o => o.Status).HasColumnName("status"), a line unchanged since stage-1.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Entity types with constructors > Read-only properties (private setters); DonHangDbContext.cs:45 @ stage-2, :44 @ stage-1

claims.text: When Cancel() changes Status on an order loaded by FindAsync (tracked), SaveChangesAsync writes status = cancelled to the orders row.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Saving data > Basic save (change tracking); verified with InMemory provider on stage-2 DonHangDbContext

claims.text: Loading an order runs none of the public constructor's checks: a stored order with no item rows loads with Items.Count == 0 and no exception.

claims.text: The public constructor's checks guard orders the code creates, not rows already in the table; a row can be written by SQL outside the application.
The private constructor sets Status to "" as a placeholder whose value never matters: EF Core replaces it with the row's value before the repository returns the order.
claims.source_hint: Entities.cs:55-58 @ stage-2; verified by the InMemory load (status = stored value)
